It bears emphasis that forum-selection clauses contained in form passage contracts are subject to judicial 
scrutiny for fundamental fairness. In this case, there is no indication that petitioner set Florida as the forum 
in which disputes were to be resolved as a means of discouraging cruise passengers from pursuing 
legitimate claims. Any suggestion of such a bad-faith motive is belied by two facts: Petitioner has its 
principal place of business in Florida, and many of its cruises depart from and return to Florida ports. 
or overreaching. Finally, respondents have conceded that they were given notice of the forum provision 
and, therefore, presumably retained the option of rejecting the contract with impunity. In the case before 
us, therefore, we conclude that the Court of Appeals erred in refusing to enforce the forum-selection 
clause.
